core_obligations: Take an ascending chain of principal ideals and factor its first element into prime powers, obtaining a finite list of primes p_1, ..., p_r (proof lines 29766-29767).

Because the chain is ascending, each later generator is an associate of a product of the same primes with exponents bounded by e_1, ..., e_r, so only finitely many classes occur (proof lines 29768-29769).
Conclude that the chain is eventually constant (proof lines 29769-29770).
proof_roadmap: Fix the prime factorization of the first element of the chain (proof lines 29765-29767).
Bound the possible later elements by the finitely many exponent vectors and conclude stabilisation (proof lines 29767-29771).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a unique factorization domain satisfies the ascending chain condition for principal ideals (statement lines 29759-29763). The proof does not argue with divisor chains or invoke Noetherianity of any kind: it factors the first element of a given ascending chain as a product of primes, then uses the containment of principal ideals to see that every later element is an associate of a product of the same primes with exponents bounded by those of the first element, so only finitely many possibilities arise (proof lines 29765-29771). The finiteness of the exponent bookkeeping, driven entirely by unique factorization, is the content. H2.
